To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the average effect of a treatment on quality of life may be small and that there may be considerable variability among individuals in the magnitude of the effect of treatment.

individual differences in treatment responses dominate the average treatment difference for quality-of-life outcomes, that individual differences are not error, and that they should be incorporated into clinical decision-making.

individual differences in health-related quality-of life treatment outcomes are large relative to average treatment effects, and that these individual differences should be incorporated into the analysis and reporting of health-related quality of-life data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the evaluation of health-related quality of-life outcomes in cancer clinical trials, with a special emphasis on individual differences in response.
the individual patient's response to treatment.
the development of statistical methods for analyzing health-related quality of-life data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the treatment effect on health-related quality-of life is small and variable.
the average treatment difference is not clinically significant, but that individual differences in treatment responses are clinically significant and should be considered in treatment decisions.
the average treatment effect is not the only effect, and it is probably not the most important one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the average treatment effect is a necessary but insufficient basis for understanding treatment impact on health-related quality-of life outcomes.

individual differences in health-related quality-of life treatment response are ubiquitous and important, and that they are best characterized by mixed-effects models that subsume both average treatment differences and the variation in individual responses.
the individual differences in treatment responses are the most important part of the story.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when health-related quality-of life data are available, they can and should be used to inform treatment decisions.
individual differences in treatment responses should be considered in health-related quality-of life analyses.
, for a given trial, it is possible to estimate the extent and nature, as well as the average, treatment effect on health-related quality-of- life outcomes.
